## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Algebra
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Algebra metric
//  - Algebra numeric
//  - Algebra operations

library Algebra
{
    //==
    // # Algebra metric
    //
    // Derived functionality for the magnitude, distance and lattice interfaces
    // (`algebra.concepts.plato`): unit-length tests, proximity predicates,
    // nearest-of selection, and the component-wise clamp
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metric_space). Shared provenance note:
    // `core.library.plato`.

    //==
    // INormed

    // True when x has unit length, within the given tolerance on the squared
    // magnitude (avoids the square root).
    IsUnit(x: INormed, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => x.MagnitudeSquared.AlmostEqual(1.0, tolerance);

    // True when x has (near) zero length, within the given squared-magnitude tolerance.
    IsZeroLength(x: INormed, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => x.MagnitudeSquared <= tolerance;

    //==
    // IMetricSpace

    // True when a and b are within the given tolerance of each other.
    IsNear(a: IMetricSpace, b: IMetricSpace, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => a.Distance(b) <= tolerance;

    // True when candidate is strictly nearer to reference than other is.
    // Example: origin.IsNearerThan(p, q) tests whether p is closer to origin than q.
    IsNearerThan(reference: IMetricSpace, candidate: IMetricSpace, other: IMetricSpace): Boolean
        => reference.Distance(candidate).LessThan(reference.Distance(other));

    // Whichever of a and b is nearer to reference (ties resolve to a).
    Nearest(reference: IMetricSpace, a: IMetricSpace, b: IMetricSpace): IMetricSpace
        => reference.Distance(a) <= reference.Distance(b) ? a : b;

    //==
    // ILattice

    // Component-wise clamp of x into the inclusive box [min, max], derived from the
    // lattice Min/Max. Assumes min <= max component-wise. (Provides the default body
    // for the IClampable.Clamp member, since IClampable inherits ILattice.)
    Clamp(x: ILattice, min: ILattice, max: ILattice): ILattice
        => x.Max(min).Min(max);

    //==
    // IDifference<TDelta> — the affine surface, derived
    //
    // `IDifference` declares only Add(Self, TDelta) and Between(Self, Self): the
    // torsor action and its inverse. Everything below follows from those two plus
    // the interface's `where TDelta: IAdditive, TDelta: IScalable` bound, so an
    // implementing type owes two members rather than the six it used to spell out
    // by hand. Point2D/Point3D and Instant previously wrote all of this per type
    // (transforms.library.plato, time.library.plato); PointN, UvCoordinate
    // and UvwCoordinate declared `implements IDifference<...>` and wrote none of
    // it, so they carried throwing stubs until these bodies existed.
    //
    // The earlier note here said Plato had no type-parameter constraint syntax and
    // that MidPoint was therefore unreachable. That was already out of date:
    // `where` clauses on interfaces are live (IInterval / IBounds in
    // intervals-bounds.concepts.plato), and MidPoint now falls out of the Lerp
    // below via IInterpolatable.

    // The position displaced by the negation of delta. The `-` spelling of
    // Add(x, -delta).
    Subtract(x: IDifference<$D>, delta: $D): IDifference<$D>
        => x.Add(delta.Negative);

    // The displacement from b to a (a - b). Same delta as Between(b, a); the `-`
    // operator spelling of position difference. Orientation follows Between.
    Subtract(a: IDifference<$D>, b: IDifference<$D>): $D
        => b.Between(a);

    // NOT derivable here: the commuted `Add(delta, position)`. A library function
    // dispatches on its FIRST parameter, which the compiler requires to be a
    // concrete type or an interface — a bare type variable is rejected with
    // "not a concrete type or interface". So reversed-operand forms over an interface
    // cannot be spelled generically at all, and any position type wanting
    // `delta + position` writes it concretely (Instant does, in
    // time.library.plato). Same reason the delta-centric `Apply(delta, position)`
    // API shape was set aside: library dispatch is on the first parameter.

    // The position a fraction `t` of the way from a to b, walked along the
    // displacement between them. t is unclamped, so it extrapolates. This is the
    // IInterpolatable obligation for every ICoordinate that is also a IDifference,
    // and it is what makes MidPoint / LerpClamped / SmoothLerp (P1, over
    // IInterpolatable) reach the position types.
    Lerp(a: IDifference<$D>, b: IDifference<$D>, t: Number): IDifference<$D>
        => a.Add(a.Between(b) * t);

    //==
    // IOriginBased<TDelta> — the last two primitives, derived
    //
    // With an origin fixed, the position space and the delta space are the same
    // space under two names, so the torsor action and its inverse are just delta
    // arithmetic with a round trip through the conversions. An IOriginBased type
    // therefore owes Offset and FromOffset and nothing else: Add and Between come
    // from here, and Subtract / Lerp from the IDifference section above.
    //
    // This is the same shape as IQuantity's Amount/FromAmount seam
    // (quantities.library.plato), one level up: there the carrier is a Number and
    // the full additive structure is transported onto Self; here the carrier is
    // the delta group and only the affine action is transported, because a
    // position deliberately does NOT gain Self + Self or a scalar multiple.

    // The position displaced by delta.
    Add(x: IOriginBased<$D>, delta: $D): IOriginBased<$D>
        => x.FromOffset(x.Offset + delta);

    // The displacement from a to b (b - a), matching the IDifference orientation.
    Between(a: IOriginBased<$D>, b: IOriginBased<$D>): $D
        => b.Offset - a.Offset;

    // The origin itself: the position at zero displacement. The receiver only
    // selects the type, and for runtime-arity positions supplies the arity.
    // Reaches TDelta's Zero through the interface's `where TDelta: IAdditive` bound
    // (Zero lives on IAdditive, not INumericalLimits, so Duration resolves too).
    Origin(x: IOriginBased<$D>): IOriginBased<$D>
        => x.FromOffset(x.Offset.Zero);

    //==
    // # Algebra numeric
    //
    // Derived functionality for the numeric tower (`algebra.concepts.plato`):
    // identity tests, blends, sign and absolute value, tolerance comparisons,
    // remapping, and the Number-concrete shaping functions
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_number). Shared provenance note:
    // `core.library.plato`.

    //==
    // INumerical

    // True when x equals the additive identity (zero).
    IsZero(x: INumerical): Boolean
        => x == x.Zero;

    // True when x equals the multiplicative identity (one).
    IsOne(x: INumerical): Boolean
        => x == x.One;

    // The weighted sum a*s + b*t of two values with scalar weights.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_combination)
    LinearCombination(a: INumerical, b: INumerical, s: Number, t: Number): INumerical
        => a * s + b * t;

    // Barycentric blend of three values: at (u,v)=(0,0) yields a, (1,0) yields b,
    // (0,1) yields c. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barycentric_coordinate_system)
    Barycentric(a: INumerical, b: INumerical, c: INumerical, u: Number, v: Number): INumerical
        => a + (b - a) * u + (c - a) * v;
```

## Reading this entry

Parameters before the colon are input values; the type after the parameter list is the result.
The first parameter also supplies the dot-call receiver. Type parameters on a declaration are
bare names; free signature variables use `$`. Read the tier and domain guides for units, frames,
